behaviorClauses.(1): MatchHostRegistry keeps { registry, recoveryRan } in one Symbol.for("mekstation.multiplayer.matchHostRegistry") slot on globalThis; getMatchHostRegistry, bootstrapMultiplayerServer and _resetMatchHostRegistry use it; the :223 comment now says what the slot gives
behaviorClauses.(2)+(3) server: rebuildHostFromActivatedBranch awaits host.replayToAttachedViewers() after markViewersForResync; ServerMatchHost runs the per-socket join replay from 0 for every attached socket (own viewer, fog filter, publication guard, delivery numbering) and stamps replacesStream: true on the ReplayStart in that push's send step, after the guard and the stamping; never broadcaster.broadcast
behaviorClauses.(3) protocol/client/hook: ReplayStartSchema gains replacesStream: z.literal(true).optional(); the client resets its delivery admission state to connect()'s initial values on the marker and emits "streamReplaced"; connectMultiplayerSession then replaces the mirror log with the replayed events (the first replayed game event replaces it; ready empties it when the replay carried none), so the old stream is never mixed in and the mirror is never empty in between

designDeviationsFromAdmission: The hook does not empty the mirror log when streamReplaced fires; it marks it for replacement and the first replayed game event REPLACES the log (ready empties it when the replay carried none). The first implementation emptied it on the event; on the intermediate build E2E-25 then failed at spec:352 (the host page lost networked-gm-correction-status) in both runs. INFERENCE for the cause: between ReplayStart and ReplayEnd the mirror was empty, NetworkedGameSurface returns MatchLoadingState when mirrorSession is null (NetworkedGameSurface.tsx:331-333), which unmounts the GM controls and their status state. The hook row now asserts the mirror is not empty between ReplayStart and the replayed body; mutant M6 (the intermediate helper) is caught by it.

The marker is stamped by a per-push safeSend wrapper in ServerMatchHost, not by a replacesStream parameter threaded through ServerMatchHostReplay.sendReplay/handleSessionJoin. The first implementation used the parameter; oxlint then measured a NEW max-lines warning on ServerMatchHostReplay.ts ("File has too many lines (411)", max 400; the baseline file lints clean), so that file was restored to HEAD and the stamp moved. Same place in the flow: after the guard and the delivery stamping, on the ReplayStart only.

Resync marks are kept after the push (the admission design said the push clears them). Reason (code reading, not measured): the existing row "viewer past N is resynced from the new head and its cursor discarded" rejoins with lastSeq/cursor 99 and expects the prefix; with the mark cleared that join would resume past the rebuilt head. The mark was kept before that row's second half was run.

The existing row's first assertion (issued === 0 right after the rebuild) pinned "nothing is sent to an attached socket", which clause (2) changes; it now asserts the push numbered the prefix from 0 and the viewer record holds exactly the pushed count (a kept record would reuse the old numbers and keep its length). src/lib/multiplayer/server/__tests__/ServerMatchHost.rewindRebuild.test.ts +18/-1.

findingsReportedNotFixed.detail: After a rewind the push renumbers each viewer from 0 (discardAll), and the durable delivery record refuses the reused numbers: every run where the rebuild reached the live match logged 8 "[ViewerDeliveryCursors] persist failed; ... SqliteError: UNIQUE constraint failed: mp_viewer_delivery.match_id, mp_viewer_delivery.player_id, mp_viewer_delivery.delivery_sequence" warnings (u22a-local-privacy-a 8, u22a-local-privacy-b 8, u22a-final-privacy-a 8, u22a-final-privacy-b 8; the baseline and M1 runs 0). Persist is best-effort, so the frames are still sent; the durable rows keep the superseded mapping. INFERENCE: a cold restart does not restore those rows for a rewound match (MatchRecovery.ts:211-212 skips restorePersistedViewerDeliveries).

A client that is not attached when the push goes out (its socket dropped just before, or it was offline) and later reconnects WITHOUT reloading still holds the superseded stream: its next SessionJoin resumes from 0 because of the resync mark (ServerMatchHost.handleSessionJoin), but that join replay carries no replace-stream marker, so the client drops it as duplicates (client.ts admitByDelivery) and blocks on the next event. A page reload works (probe M3). rewind-pack E2E-44 "offline player catches up after rewind" is a strict expected failure on both the baseline and the final tree (ladder).
